title: Schemas of Marital Change: From Arranged Marriages to Eloping for Love
venue: Journal of Marriage and the Family
treatment: schemas linking marital change to foreign/global influence and modernity
outcome: shift from arranged marriage to love marriage/elopement
reason: Interviews elicit beliefs attributing the rise of love marriage to foreign influence and modernization, with marriage arrangement as the outcome; abstract states structural and ideational factors are integrated, not separated.

title: Social Change, Premarital Nonfamily Experience, and Spouse Choice in an Arranged Marriage Society
authors: Dirgha J. Ghimire; William G. Axinn; Scott T. Yabiku; Arland Thornton
treatment: premarital nonfamily experience, especially media exposure and youth-club participation
outcome: participation in choice of first spouse
reason: Media exposure and nonfamily experience predict the shift away from arranged marriage toward conjugal spouse choice; channel reading equally live.

title: Marriage Timing in Nepal: Organizational Effects and Individual Mechanisms
treatment: neighbourhood nonfamily organizations (schools, health providers, employers, cinemas) and individual nonfamily experience
outcome: timing of first marriage
reason: Exposure to modern nonfamily institutions in rural Nepal as a determinant of marriage timing, with individual mechanisms tested.

title: Television and family demography: Evidence from a natural experiment in East Germany
treatment: residence-based ability to receive Western television in the GDR
outcome: marriage, childbirth, divorce; family attitudes
reason: Signal-geography natural experiment within one economy attributes reduced marriage and childbearing to Western TV role models via attitude change.

title: Postmarital Living Arrangements in Historically Patrilocal Settings: Integrating Household Fission and Migration Perspectives
authors: Jessica Pearlman; Lisa D. Pearce; Dirgha J. Ghimire; Prem Bhandari; Taylor W. Hargrove
treatment: young men's schooling, media exposure, and travel outside the natal community
outcome: departure from the extended natal household and formation of an independent household
reason: Nonfamily-exposure measures predict nuclear residence in rural Nepal while community market and employment access and household wealth are separately modelled.

title: Issues of marriage timing in different cultural contexts
venue: Carolina Digital Repository (University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill)
treatment: ideational/normative marriage attitudes and marriage-arrangement autonomy alongside economic resources
outcome: marriage timing and post-marital schooling
reason: Estimates ideational versus economic determinants of marriage timing and love-versus-arranged marriage in Nepal, a family-formation outcome in scope.

title: Does Internet Adoption Decrease Child Marriage Prevalence in Indonesia?
authors: Nur Dwiana Sari Saudi; Randi Kurniawan; Novat Pugo Sambodo; Salman Samir
treatment: household internet access, instrumented by regional signal quality
outcome: child marriage prevalence
reason: Internet exposure and delayed marriage in Indonesia; media-model and pure-channel readings both live, so tagged shared with A.20 under the dual-home rule.

title: Does Electrification Spur the Fertility Transition? Evidence From Indonesia
authors: Michael Grimm; Robert Sparrow; Luca Tasciotti
treatment: electrification-induced exposure to television
outcome: fertility preferences and realized fertility decline
reason: television exposure identified as a key channel to fertility preferences and births; channel and depicted-model readings both live

title: The impact of television and radio on reproductive behavior and on HIV / AIDS knowledge and behavior.
authors: Charles F. Westoff; Dawn Koffman; Caroline Moreau
treatment: frequency of television and radio exposure across 48 developing countries
outcome: contraceptive use, desired number of children, recent births
reason: Media exposure framed as a window onto modern life competing with traditional marriage and childbearing values, with associations persisting net of schooling, wealth and urban residence; channel reading equally live so shared with A.20.

title: The Association of Television and Radio with Reproductive Behavior
treatment: frequency of television and radio exposure
outcome: contraceptive use, desired number of children, recent fertility
reason: Media exposure across 48 developing countries linked to fertility and desired family size, with the effect attributed to depicted modern-family life; content unmeasured so the channel reading is equally live.

title: The Multifaceted Impact of Education on Fertility: Unpacking the “BASIC” Effects in China
treatment: years of education, instrumented, decomposed into base/ambition/spouse/income/concept channels
outcome: number of children, parity progression, fertility intentions
reason: Design explicitly separates a 'concept' (ideational) channel of schooling from income and work-status returns (Wall 5)

title: From Privilege to Prevalence: Contextual Effects of Women’s Schooling on African Marital Timing
treatment: cohort-level prevalence of women's schooling (contextual, net of own schooling)
outcome: age at first marriage
reason: Contextual schooling effect on marital timing of women whose own schooling did not change, isolating a social-meaning rather than own-return channel.

title: A search for aggregate-level effects of education on fertility, using data from Zimbabwe
treatment: district-level average schooling and literacy, net of own education
outcome: birth hazards, fertility desires, contraceptive use
reason: Estimates aggregate education spillovers on women whose own schooling did not change, controlling own education and urbanization — the ideational-content design of Wall 5.

title: Harmony in diplomacy, convergence in choices: Low fertility diffusion through Sino‐Korean normalization
treatment: 1992 Sino-Korean diplomatic normalization opening contact with low-fertility South Korea
outcome: fertility and marriage rates among Korean Chinese
reason: Contact with an external modern reference society is the exposure, with adoption of its low-fertility norms as the stated mechanism.

title: Societal transitions, ethnolinguistic identities, and marital conservatism in Central Asia
venue: Journal of Marriage and the Family
treatment: Russian linguo-cultural exposure and post-Soviet Western influence measured ethnolinguistically
outcome: attitudes to premarital chastity, optimal marriage age, parental role in marriage, endogamy, divorce
reason: Exposure to an external (Russian/Western) family model predicts marital-conservatism norms net of education, religiosity, and urbanicity in Kyrgyzstan.

title: Competing Family Pathways for Immigrants and Their Descendants in Germany
treatment: immigrant generation and origin-group exposure to German host family norms
outcome: cohabitation, marriage, first birth
reason: Event-history study of convergence with native partnership and fertility pathways across migrant generations and cohorts.

title: Coming Out of the Penumbras: World Culture and Cross-National Variation in Divorce Rates
treatment: embeddedness in world culture / global institutions carrying a modern family model
outcome: national divorce rates
reason: Explicit developmental-idealism and world-society estimand: global cultural influence predicts divorce rates across 84 countries net of controls; outcome is family dissolution rather than births.

title: Impacts of Migration on Marriage Arrangement: A Comparison of Turkish Families in Turkey and Western Europe
treatment: migration to Western Europe and migrant generation (exposure to host family model)
outcome: arranged versus couple-initiated marriage (spouse choice)
reason: Compares migrants to stayers with the difference widening by generation and only partly explained by education, i.e. convergence with exposure to a Western family model.

title: The impact of outmigration of men on fertility and marriage in the migrant-sending states of Mexico, 1995–2000
treatment: municipal level of male outmigration to the US
outcome: total fertility and proportion of women married
reason: Migration exposure associated with marriage decline net of sex ratio and education, attributed to changing family-formation ideas.

title: Freedom of Partner Choice in Togo
treatment: exposure to Western conjugal family model via mission schooling, education, and mass media
outcome: individual freedom of partner choice vs arranged marriage
reason: Tests convergence of Togolese nuptiality toward an imported Western conjugal family system, with partner choice as the family-formation outcome.

title: Fertility attitudes and behavior of Saudi Arabian students enrolled in U.S. universities
authors: Khalid A. A. Al‐Mubarak; Donald J. Adamchak
treatment: length of stay studying in U.S. universities
outcome: fertility attitudes and number of children
reason: Direct residence in a Western setting is among the modelled determinants of fertility attitudes and behaviour among Saudi nationals.

title: A Reappraisal of the Status of Women and Nuptiality in Sub-Saharan Africa
treatment: westernization, migration, and women's education in sub-Saharan Africa
outcome: nuptiality regimes and marriage arrangements
reason: Explicitly assesses whether Western contact altered African nuptiality regimes, reporting a largely null selective-adoption finding.
